summary: Round 8 retest of the Stops Board bugs from iteration 6, run in the browser at /api/dashboard/stops as admin. All 3 bugs are fixed and the regressions pass. (1) HIGH, socket rejoin after token expiry, both paths tested live. (a) 'io server disconnect': a 15 s admin JWT was put in localStorage.accessToken along with a real refreshToken. The board showed Live, then 'Reconnecting…' for about 1 s at 16 s, then Live again. There was a single /auth/refresh call (the two sockets share it) and both sockets (StopsBoard and ArrivalNotices) reopened at 16.0 and 16.2 s. A PUT /drivers/4/stops adding a TEST_ stop showed on the card (1/4) 0.84 s later. A second run with a 12 s token showed the arrival toast arriving-notice-23 straight after the rejoin, so the ArrivalNotices socket rejoins too. (b) connect_error 'Invalid token': with the board Live, accessToken was swapped for an expired token that has a valid signature, then fleet-preview-proxy was restarted. socket.io's automatic reconnect at 1.2-1.9 s was refused. At 4.3 s (the 3 s rejoin delay) came /auth/me 401, then /auth/refresh 200, then /auth/me 200, the sockets reopened, and Live was back at 5.06 s. A PUT afterwards updated the card in 0.83 s. A garbage or expired token at page load also reached Live within about 1 s. (2) MEDIUM trip:cancelled: Sarah started a TEST trip (id 26) and the badge showed 'On trip since 1:04 PM'. After admin POST /trips/26/cancel the badge cleared in 0.51 s. (3) MEDIUM mobile: at 390px scrollWidth is 390 (was 401), every card spans 16-374 px, no element overflows, and Maria's long airport address is cut off with an ellipsis. (4) LOW date: Michael's badge reads 'On trip since Feb 8, 8:30 AM'. Regression: Sarah's arrival at Chase Field showed the toast in 0.09 s ('Sarah Johnson arrived · Chase Field, Phoenix, AZ · confirmed by driver · 0 m from the stop'), flashed the card green and moved progress to 2/3 in 0.51 s. tsc is clean and backend vitest passes 157/157. Data restored: Sarah has Zoo arrived, Chase Field next and qqzz pending, and her destination is Chase Field. Trip 26 and its 3 trip_photos rows are deleted by id. Vehicle 4's odometer is 12010. John, Maria and Michael's trip 6 were not touched.

issues: Touch targets are bigger but still under 44 px: stops-board-edit-<id> is now 69x32 (was 53x16), and the show-idle label is 210x20 with a 16x16 checkbox.

action_items: LOW: StopsBoard.tsx:81-91 and ArrivalNotices.tsx:36-48: the rejoin setTimeouts are not cleared on unmount. If the user leaves the board within 1-3 s of a server close or refused handshake, rejoin() still calls socket.connect() and reopens a socket that nothing will close (its listeners keep calling load and setLive). Keep the timer id and clear it in cleanup, or check a 'disposed' flag before connect(). StopsBoard's cleanup should also call socket.removeAllListeners(), as ArrivalNotices does.
LOW: the rejoin logic is the same in both components (about 12 lines). Move it into one shared socket hook or context. That would also bring the tab down from 2-3 sockets to 1.
LOW: the indicator says 'Reconnecting…' forever after an error the code does not retry (for example 'Dashboard access is limited…'). Show 'Offline' when socket.active is false.
LOW: raise the mobile touch targets to 44 px (Edit stops button, show-idle label).
critical_code_review_comments: The rejoin design is sound. The auth callback reads localStorage on every connect. rejoin() makes a REST call, so an expired token goes through the axios refresh flow. Concurrent refreshes are combined into one (seen as a single /auth/refresh for both sockets). If the refresh token is expired, the interceptor sends the user to /login, which stops the loop. A deleted user gets a 401 on the retried request, which clears the tokens and redirects. 'unavailable' (outage) keeps retrying every 3 s, which is acceptable.

The connect_error regex /token|Authentication|User not found/ also matches 'Authentication required' (no token). That case ends in the interceptor's login redirect, so it cannot loop forever while the page is open.
Cleanup does not clear the rejoin timers (see action_items). It is minor, but it can leak a socket.
